The argossians would immediately agree to point 1,4 and 5, but the following issued and solutions would be identified and proposed with regards to the other 2 points.
[list]
2: The argossians would refuse to cooperate with the isolationists and restorationists, citing their past and current  oppression of Aboriginal Argossians. The tribal leaders would state that, in their opinion, the restorationists and isolationists would only hinder their fight against tyranny and their independence movement. As a solution, the argossians would simply state that they would only form a united front with the democrats.

3: The Argossians would refuse to give up their freedom and independence to any unfamiliar external force. As a solution to this they would propose that a central command structure be set up, to jointly coordinate strategic moves and planning, but the operation of units and whether they agreed to the orders of the command structure would be up for decision by their respective government.
[/list]
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=Operation Haiyan]
[b]Luwakki offensive[/b]
The attack westwards would easily cut off the supply lines of the Luwakki units, but by this point they would already be well within the democratic salient, using Guerilla tactics to take key supply lines and other infrastructure. Despite this, with nobody protecting the town of Luwakki anymore, the pocket would fall once again. Trapping the units deep within democratic territory and putting an effective end to the offensives original goals. Now, the soldiers only focus would be getting out of the salient alive.

The tanks, planes and change of tactics would all contribute to the destruction of the operation. As supply routes were refortified, the Guerilla units would no longer have enough manpower to capture them. From this point, it would only go downhill, with the tanks and planes now easily picking off the small units. In the end, none would make it out alive, further securing the democrats offensive, which was now rapidly barreling towards Astan, with no sign of stopping.

[b]Race to the south[/b]
The decision to spread out instead of forming thin salients would be effective. With a much larger area to attack, the isolationists would not be able to use their Guerilla tactics, instead having to once again resort to attrition to keep the democrats at bay. This would result in many troops simply being gunned down by pax international of being bombed by Qianxun aircraft.

Civilian operations would also be very effective. At this point in the war, many people simply wanted the fighting over, not caring who got them out of it. As such, there would be little who refused to collaborate and those that didnt immediately would be coerced. As for gangs, the closer and closer the Democratic army got to Astan, the more thriving the gang culture became. In the settlements around Astan, high-profile drug traffickers and gang leaders would rise to the task of administering their towns on behalf of summitONE. Additionally, many gang members would be easily recruited into the ranks of the Democratic army, helping replace the Vespurias and Qianxun.

Over the course of a week, the relentless attacks by the Democratic army would bring them to capture Astan. General Kaiwai, now realising that he could only delay the inevitable, would secretly evacuate the city, along with his top commanders. They would travel through the night to avoid suspicion and would eventually reach a small village, Munolui, in the middle of the Astaniran country side, where they would set up a new, more covert base of operations. The capture of Astan would give the democrats access to an abundance of ports and other infrastructure, but would also give them the challenge of administering the impoverished, war-torn population.
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=Yellow bay]
The democrats would be able to see the oblivious nationalist navy from miles away, before the nationalists even knew they were somewhat close to the democrats. This upper-hand in technology would give the democrats a powerful advantage against the nationalists. Additionally, the democrats would far outnumber and overpower their opponents, making the battle effectively one-sided.

The subsonic cruise missiles would take the nationalists by surprise, as they had only just detected the Democratic fleet mere moments ago. The lone submarine would be immediately taken out by the strike, drowning its crew. On the surface, the nationalists would have better luck, firing a huge counterstrike consisting of tens of large, clunky missiles and round of fire from the battleships canons.

However, the democrats would be far ahead in technology. Their modern missile capabilities would be fatal to the nationalist ships, who possessed no defence or counter against the missiles. Most ships would begin to sink within 30 minutes of the intial engagement, whilst those that survived would be ordered to retreat, so that the nationalists could consolidate their forces and make a renewed offensive. This would allow the democrats to easily take swaths of eastern coastline, once again allowing them access to port infrastructure.
[/spoiler]

[nation]Nordiheim[/nation]
[nation]Pantagruel[/nation][/quote]
[b]All that remains[/b]

Freya Moran's 1st Maneuver Army, despite having been positioned towards the far west of the invasion force, would somehow be the first to march triumphantly into the Astaniran capital city, with Astaniran Democratic troops proudly flying both the Astaniran national flag and the communist banners of the Astaniran Social Party. Moran herself would order no Pax International-branded vehicles or personnel to take part in the initial entry into Astan, fearing a loss in propaganda value should foreign troops be photographed during the capture of the city. For many men, the "liberation" of the national capital would represent the definitive end of the war and the mending of divisions.

However, things were never that easy.

First, the matter of Astan itself. Thanks to the rapid speed of events, the city would be spared of a protracted, destructive siege, but the humanitarian crisis that had been concealed by the Isolationists would just now rear its ugly head before the Democratic movement. Astan had effectively been converted into a fortified citadel, enclosed from the outside world, stuck in time from decades of degradation from past tragedies that only now had become unfrozen for Pax Int'l to see. Corpses littered the streets, not felled by bullets and shrapnel but by hunger and disease, their bones breaking out of their paper thin skin. No animals remained in the city, most having been converted into frozen meals to alleviate the hunger of the many.

Then came shelter, of which there was little. A few hospitals here and there, maybe a still-extant university campus could still reliably provide water and electricity, but all that remained were concrete shells, barely worthy of even being called shelter, dotted with bullet holes and bomb craters, windowless, seemingly on the precipice of some horrific collapse, just waiting to be brought down by either a ferocious tsunami, or else a brutal military offensive by yet another party. The ports at least were still serviceable, though they were completely dominated by the Astaniran warlords. Fisheries, oil rigs, desalination plants, everything that could possibly be used to prolong a man's life was in the hands of one gang or another.

All that remains now were the few people who waited in their homes or in the homes of a stranger. Moran, completely ill-prepared to take up the role of a city administrator, would hurriedly ask the aid of the popular committees in setting up a new municipal government as soon as possible.

Neither City Hall nor the Government Palace were serviceable for coordinating relief efforts, and so the 1st Maneuver Army would instead set up shop at the University of Astan's campus grounds, an [i]ad hoc[/i] headquarters forming in the university's chemistry department. Pax International troops would be sent to quarter in the humanities building, while native Astanirans would rest in the computer laboratories and mathematics department. 

Freya Moran would be swiftly appointed as the nominal mayor of Astan, and would began redistricting the city into a network of zones that centered primarily around the most prominent standing buildings in the city. From this makeshift redistricting, Moran would prioritize zones that were worse off, with warlords and popular commitee delegates alike being formally appointed to serve in local boards to encourage the resumption of economic activity and reconstruction. A chief prosecutor would be set up as well to immediately restore the city's judiciary, chiefly to manage complaints over the division of aid, while in the streets Pax International would serve alongside gangsters and soviet militiamen as a restored municipal police force to curb mob violence and looting.

Back in Kuwalkti, David Cyriacus would order the CEDC to take up their new posts in Astan and leave Kuwalkti in the hands of SummitONE. Horano Benir, believing that victory was near, would enthusiastically agree and depart for Astan together with the entire Committee of Executives and the Conciliar Guard.

While 1st Maneuver Army would settle inside Astan, 2nd and 5th Maneuver Armies under Edwin Roylance and Bai He would prosecute their steady southern advance to finish what little objectives remained until the completion of Operation Haiyan. Roylance, exasperated at having his own advance delayed by several critical days thanks to the Luwakki offensive, would be particularly aggressive in his advance, copying Moran's own encirclement campaign and taking full advantage of superior Qianxun armor to score several key victories against the Isolationist forces, most of whom seem to have virtually abandoned much of East Astanir followed General Kawai's own evacuation.

However, by now Pax International seems to have reached its breaking point. Vespurian and Qianxun soldiers have begun signing off their contracts and rotating out, with most relocating north to serve in defensive positions, their roles filled up by less effective Astaniran recruits collected from the popular committees and the gangs. Most of these native troops, while generally far more aggressive and driven to succeed than foreign soldiers of fortune, were also less capable in marksmanship, with limited understanding of critical first aid, and having poorer discipline in the management of supplies and field rations. Training them would take time and money, two resources which thankfully Moran was able to afford them with her capture of Astan.

It was only until the middle of May that Pax Int'l would finally succeed in capturing the entire eastern section of the Astaniran mainland, making the Democratic movement the largest faction in the civil war by territory alone. The campaign had been won, and Operation Haiyan would become the first successful military operation in modern Qianxun history after years of peaceful isolation, with war scholars and analysts flocking from the University of Qianxun Project 661 Campus to research Pax International's prosecution of war.

At this juncture, the so-called "Democratic Navy" that had been fighting under Admiral Yun Caibo would at last cease to fly the Astaniran flag, instead flying the Qianxun flag and making its full intentions known to the enemy, even if it had been obvious from the start. The Qianxun were no longer simply just adventurers and interventionists trying to protect a small rebel group, but a legitimate geopolitical ally of a true nation state in the form of East Astanir. Now was the time to reflect that, to "Astanirize" the culture of the nation's armed forces from Qianxun and Vespurian influence after all these months of fighting.

As Qianxun and Democratic forces began to consolidate, back in the north David Cyriacus would intervene in the talks with the Argossians, clarifying certain points, such as that the united front was not to involve the Isolationists and Restorationists that have caused them so much misery, and that the Argossians will be permitted their own independence in military affairs, with the supreme council to only just be an advisory body to coordinate military strategy. The final push was now needed, a grand, forcing advance to the west to crush all remaining opposition to Democratic Astanir.

[quote=gythena;60517005][spoiler][b][i]36 miles outside the city of Eluoja, 7:48, West Elseyran Time[/i][/b]

On the [i]GNV Sotavasarasat[/i] sat a Captain Tapio, reading a book in his Captains Quarters. Outside, it snowed gently upon Gythenas waters, a sign of winters recession and the coming of the months of sunlight. He looked up from his book and gazed into the outside.

How gently the waters moved and swayed with spirit, almost as if alive and carrying the ship across the seas with its grace. Said waters were Gythenas bane and benefit, taking people across the waters while cracking its whip across the coast from time to time.

Suddenly, commotion was heard from below Tapios deck, sounding akin to stomping and rushed movements. Tapio stood up and looked out his front-view window down to bow side.

He didnt see much, just the front of the ship and the pale blue sea. He was about to sit back down to his book when he heard louder banging from under the deck. He froze for a solid 20 seconds, listening in for more noises, before deciding to walk to the door to check what was up.

All of a sudden, Tapios own Coast Guard troops were rushing up the stairs and up to his quarters. Tapio was quickly outmatched and put his hands up as the men burst through the door, aiming their assault rifles at their captain and reorganizing. One of the soldiers piped up:
Surrender control of the vessel immediately and we will let the rest of the crew and you leave with your lives. Make your choice.

Tapio was in shock, thinking, [i]what? Why are my troops going against my command? What is happening in Gythena to cause such a rebellion? Did we get raided by pirates?[/i] Nevertheless, he conceded to the soldiers commands and gave control of the ship to them. The soldiers quickly took to the command board and began handing the ship.

Where are we headed now?
Eluoja. They wont be expecting our arrival, the ships at harbor will be easy targets. If the men on the Raivoa are successful, we will tell them we are headed there
Dont. Fire. At the ships. Some of those are foreign property and we cant afford to make enemies out of anyone if we want any of our efforts to go anywhere. Besides, the element of surprise might be enough considering were have at least one ship suddenly aiming at their port.

Tapio simply sat in his chair, surrounded by armed men ready to fire at any moment, while he contemplated it all.
[i]Pyhä, what is going on[/i]
He simply sat there in his chair, surrounded by armed men ready to fire at any moment. He looked at the future with confusion and concern, as the ship turned around and prepared its arsenal.
[/spoiler][/quote]
The Sanguinians entered the city of Polijamsa, but not before making a headcount of their available men. Don Cirino was initially jubilant to venture into the cold of the northern earth, but now he seemed less ecstatic. A single drop of sweat formed on his forehead though the weather was still frigid. They were meant to be a Great Red Embassy showcasing the best that the Sanguinians had to offer, and so their numbers were rather large for a typical delegation. Economists, social workers, environmentalists, socialist theoreticians, all numbering some 900 something men that were meant to supplant preexisting Sanguinian personnel who were still loyal to the Serenissima, the old Sanguinan government.

"And guarding these 900," said Ulf de Mayne, pointing to his men who flanked the spread out components of the delegation like a great legion, ", is in total 3,000 personnel of MROS Dynamics aboard all the passenger ferries. The ships themselves have the slightest bit of naval capabilities because of the guns we had installed on 'em, but nothing too fancy."

"That's... that's not good..." Don Cirino said, almost comically gulping in fear. "What is the Socialist Ethics Commission saying? Shouldn't we be pulling out now?"

"Cui Fang?... he says to remain here and stick to our main objectives. If the Gythenan government is unable or unwilling to coordinate with us on the scheduled talks, then we'll have to presume that they are in no capacity to govern their own country."

"A-And if they're not of capacity?"

"We'll begin the revolution from here then." Ulf said bluntly, pointing to the Gythenan coast. "Intelligence has informed us that something strange has happened in the Gythenan area of responsibility. Don Cirino, please understand that we came here with the intent of forming a last friendship with the Gythenan, but also 3,000 men and women under my personal command, armed and deputized by the order of the International in order to safeguard Mr. Almstedt and Socialist International's shared interests. In the mean time though, we need to disperse. Before our presence becomes too suspect. You have the list of resorts?"

"Yes, yes!" Don Cirino responded, quickly taking out his phone and showing his bookings. "Here, we're all set to stay at th-..."

"Whatever, let's just head there now." Ulf interrupted, suddenly walking forwards toward the city itself, speaking carefully into his headpiece. "Everyone, this is Lighthouse 6. I have no idea what's going on, but it seems like Gythena is experiencing unforeseen political events. Until we can confirm exactly what the hell is going on, everyone is advised to head to their respective bookings. Wear plain clothes and conceal your gear in your bags. Don't identify yourselves as members of the Sanguinian delegation if you can, since Mr. Almstedt still expects us to gain something out of this even if things turn to sh-t. Out."
